metadata.name: Ecodesign for Python
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules specific to Python code: sober ORM (Django/SQLAlchemy), generators, vectorisation, bounded caches, reused connections.

donnees.name: Python — data access
donnees.description: Django ORM / SQLAlchemy: transfer and materialise only what is needed (RGESN Backend, GR491_Backend_2/3).

rules.title: N+1 query on a walked queryset
rules.description: Iterating a queryset whose associations you read fires one query per row: network and database cost grow linearly with the volume.
rules.recommendation: Load the associations you walk with select_related/prefetch_related (Django) or joinedload/selectinload (SQLAlchemy).

rules.title: Unbounded queryset materialised
rules.description: `.all()` or `list(...)` on an unbounded table loads every row into application memory.
rules.recommendation: Paginate every exposed list; stream large volumes with iterator() (Django) or yield_per() (SQLAlchemy).

rules.title: Project the fields you need
rules.description: Loading whole objects when only two columns are read transfers and deserialises data for nothing.
rules.recommendation: Use only()/defer()/values()/values_list() (Django) or load_only() (SQLAlchemy) to fetch just the columns you use.

rules.title: Group bulk writes
rules.description: One save() per row inside a loop produces one database round trip per record.
rules.recommendation: bulk_create/bulk_update (Django), executemany or batched insert() (SQLAlchemy); bound the batch size.

memoire.name: Python — memory and streams
memoire.description: Do not materialise in memory what can be streamed (RGESN Algorithms, GR491_Backend_4).

rules.title: File read entirely into memory
rules.description: read() and readlines() load the whole file; memory grows with the file size, up to swapping or an OOM.
rules.recommendation: Iterate the file line by line, or read in blocks (read(size), iter_content) for large volumes.

rules.title: pandas: row-by-row loop instead of vectorising
rules.description: iterrows() and apply(axis=1) run Python per row: one to two orders of magnitude more costly than the equivalent vectorised operation.
rules.recommendation: Vectorise with numpy and pandas operations; cut memory with suitable dtypes (category, short integers).

rules.title: String concatenation in a loop
rules.description: `s += ...` rebuilds the whole string on every iteration (quadratic behaviour on long sequences).
rules.recommendation: Accumulate in a list then ''.join(...), or write straight to a stream.

rules.title: Membership test on a large list
rules.description: `x in list` is linear; repeated inside a loop, the processing turns quadratic.
rules.recommendation: Index into a set or a dict before the loop (constant-time lookup).

io.name: Python — I/O, network and cache
io.description: Reuse connections, bound caches, do not poll in a loop (RGESN Backend/Hosting).

rules.title: Unbounded cache
rules.description: An lru_cache with no maxsize, or a global dict used as a cache, grows without limit: memory held for entries never reused.
rules.recommendation: Bound and expire every cache: lru_cache(maxsize=N), a TTL on the Redis or Memcached side.

rules.title: HTTP connections not reused
rules.description: requests.get() opens a connection, and a TLS handshake, on every call: network and CPU cost repeated for nothing.
rules.recommendation: Reuse a requests.Session (or a shared httpx client); go async for concurrent I/O.

rules.title: Polling loop
rules.description: A sleep-plus-request loop consumes CPU, network and energy continuously, even when nothing changes.
rules.recommendation: Prefer event-driven triggering (webhook, message, notification); failing that, widen the interval substantially.
